chunks: And what we have mentioned was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Khurrazad, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Abi Sa'id, who said:
I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام say: When a woman dies among a group of people among whom she has no mahram, they pour water over her. And if a man dies among women among whom he has no mahram...

Abu Hanifah said: They should pour water over him. So Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: Rather, it is permissible for them to touch of him whatever it was permissible for them to look at of him while he was alive. Then when they reach the place at which it was not permissible for them to look while he was alive, nor to touch it, they should pour water over him.

So what this report includes regarding the permissibility of a woman washing, of a man, those parts at which it was permissible for her to look while he was alive is to be understood as recommendation, and the basis is what we have stated previously.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation, indicating a preferred but non-obligatory understanding
key_terms.مَحْرَمٌ: a person within the prohibited degrees of marriage whose presence changes rulings of bodily contact and viewing
key_terms.يَصُبُّونَ: they pour water, referring to performing washing without direct touching
key_terms.يَمْسَسْنَ: they touch, referring to physical contact with the deceased body
key_terms.يَنْظُرْنَ: they look, referring to what may lawfully be seen of the body

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man or woman dies in travel and only unrelated members of the opposite sex are present?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for washing the dead when a deceased man or woman is among unrelated members of the opposite sex and no mahram is present. It distinguishes between parts of the body that may be touched and seen and those that may not, while the compiler concludes that the apparent allowance is to be understood as recommended conduct within the broader legal framework.
